note: The three para and teacher relationship tools that published 2026-09-28. These sit on the Working Together shelf. Written as TDI voice: the comments explain why the tool is built the way it is, and the questions ask the reader something. No post claims a classroom moment, because nobody is behind these accounts to answer for one.

posts: Fill it in before the conversation, with your best guess in every box. A teacher reacting to something concrete is a far easier ask than a teacher answering an open question about expectations.
Five questions rather than fifteen, on purpose. It is built for the length of conversation that can actually happen, standing up, between two blocks.
Of the five questions on the form, which one would you most want answered in the room you are in right now?
If you handed this to a teacher tomorrow, which box would be the hardest one to let them see your guess on?
The first section asks what happened, not why it happened. Motive is the part we get wrong most often, and naming it early tends to end a conversation before it has started.

There is a step for deciding whether an administrator needs to be involved, and wording for raising it so it does not land as a complaint. Jumping straight to that step is usually what makes it land as one.
Where does it usually break down for you, working out what actually happened, or having the conversation afterwards?
What has helped you tell the difference between a problem that is missing norms and a problem that is missing respect?
The lines are written out word for word deliberately. Knowing you ought to offer help is not the difficult part. Having a sentence ready that does not come out sounding like criticism is.
None of these need the teacher to agree to anything first. That is the constraint the whole card is built around, because a para often has no way to call a meeting.
Which of the four moments is the one you tend to let go past without saying anything?
What is a line that has worked for you when you needed information nobody thought to give you?
